answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 10 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. The raven multiplier is published, charged in dune, and willow lists each payment. A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, since the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. A farm of 1660 identities would post 3516 proofs and burn roughly 46 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
